formulas.tex: \text{Optimise } Z = ax + by \text{ subject to linear constraints and } x\ge0,\ y\ge0

note.en: points of R are feasible solutions; outside R, infeasible

formulas.tex: \text{test } (0, 0) \text{ in } ax + by\le c \text{ to decide which side of the line to shade}

note.en: if the line passes through the origin, test another point such as (1, 0)

formulas.tex: \text{If } R \text{ is bounded, } Z_{\max} \text{ and } Z_{\min} \text{ exist and occur at corner points of } R
\text{find corners} \to \text{evaluate } Z \text{ at each} \to \text{pick the largest / smallest}
M = \max_{\text{corners}} Z \text{ is the maximum} \iff \{ax + by > M\}\cap R = \varnothing
m = \min_{\text{corners}} Z \text{ is the minimum} \iff \{ax + by < m\}\cap R = \varnothing
Z(P) = Z(Q) = Z_{\text{opt}} \text{ at adjacent corners} \Rightarrow \text{every point of } PQ \text{ is optimal}

note.en: happens when Z is parallel to the edge PQ

formulas.tex: Z = px + qy \text{ equal at } (x_1, y_1), (x_2, y_2) \iff p(x_1 - x_2) = q(y_2 - y_1)
a_1x + b_1y = c_1,\ a_2x + b_2y = c_2 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{c_1b_2 - c_2b_1}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1},\ y = \dfrac{a_1c_2 - a_2c_1}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}
